arrays.title: Array Foundations
arrays.summary: An array in Java is a fixed-size object that stores multiple values of the same declared type and provides indexed access to its elements.
learningObjectives: Understand why arrays are fixed in size.
Understand that arrays are objects in Java.
Understand primitive arrays and reference-type arrays.
Understand default values for array elements.
Understand the difference between null and an empty array.
explanation: In one line: An array is a fixed-size Java object that stores multiple values of the same declared type.
Array elements are accessed using zero-based indexes, so the first element is at index 0.
The length of an array is fixed when the array is created and cannot be changed later.
Arrays are objects in Java, and an array variable stores a reference to the array object.
Arrays can store primitive values such as int and double or references such as String and custom objects.
Java automatically initializes every newly created array with a type-specific default value.

paragraphs: An array allows multiple values to be stored under a single variable name.
All elements belong to the array's declared component type.
An array has a fixed length, which means its size cannot be increased or decreased after creation.
Each element can be accessed directly using its index.
detailSections.note: Think of an array as a fixed number of numbered storage locations where every location has the same declared type.

arrays.title: Creating and Initializing Arrays
arrays.summary: Java provides several ways to declare, create, and initialize arrays depending on whether the size or initial values are already known.
learningObjectives: Understand what happens when an array is reassigned.
explanation: Declaring an array creates a reference variable but does not create the array object.
The new keyword creates the actual array object and determines its length.
An array initializer can create and populate an array when the values are already known.
An anonymous array can be created directly when passing an array to a method.
An array variable can later be reassigned to another array object.

detailSections.title: Declaration
paragraphs: Declaration creates an array reference variable.

String[] names;

detailSections.title: Creation with new
paragraphs: The new keyword creates the actual array object.
When using new, the array length must be specified.

String[] names = new String[3];

detailSections.title: Initialization with values
paragraphs: When the values are already known, an array initializer can create and populate the array.
The compiler determines the array length from the number of supplied values.
detailSections.codeExample:
int[] numbers = {10, 20, 30, 40};
String[] names = {"Asha", "Ravi", "John"};

arrays.title: Traversing Arrays
arrays.summary: Array traversal means visiting elements one by one, commonly using a traditional for loop or an enhanced for loop.
learningObjectives: Traverse arrays using traditional for loops.
Understand when indexed loops are preferable.
explanation: Traversal means visiting each element of an array.
A traditional for loop is useful when the index is required.
An enhanced for loop is useful when only the element value is required.
Reverse traversal starts from length - 1 and moves toward index 0.

detailSections.title: Traditional for loop
paragraphs: A traditional for loop gives access to both the index and the element.
It is useful when the index is needed or when elements must be modified by position.

detailSections.title: Enhanced for loop
paragraphs: The enhanced for loop visits every element without explicitly managing an index.
It is convenient for read-only traversal.

detailSections.title: Reverse traversal
paragraphs: Reverse traversal starts from the last valid index and moves backward.
The condition must ensure that index 0 is processed.

table.title: Choosing the right traversal

arrays.title: One-Dimensional Arrays
arrays.summary: A one-dimensional array stores elements in a single indexed sequence and can contain primitive values or references to objects.
learningObjectives: Work with arrays of custom objects.
Understand null elements in reference arrays.
explanation: A one-dimensional array stores elements in a single sequence of indexes.
Primitive arrays store values such as int, double, and char.
Reference arrays store references to objects such as String or custom classes.
Creating a reference array does not automatically create the objects referenced by its elements.

detailSections.title: Primitive arrays
paragraphs: Primitive arrays directly store primitive values.
Each element receives the default value for its primitive type when the array is created.

detailSections.title: Reference arrays
paragraphs: Reference arrays store references to objects rather than the objects themselves.
A newly created reference array contains null references until objects are assigned.

detailSections.title: Arrays of custom objects
paragraphs: An object array can store references to instances of a custom class.
The array and the objects stored through its references are separate objects.

Use reference arrays when a fixed number of object references is required.
Use one-dimensional arrays when the data naturally forms a single sequence.

arrays.title: Multidimensional and Jagged Arrays

The outer array represents rows, while each inner array represents the elements in a row.
Rows can have different lengths, so Java supports jagged arrays.

arrays.title: Searching Arrays
arrays.summary: Array searching means locating an element or determining whether a value exists. The two basic approaches are linear search and binary search.
learningObjectives: Know why binary search requires sorted data.
explanation: Linear search checks elements one by one until the target is found or the array ends.
Linear search does not require the array to be sorted.
Binary search repeatedly divides a sorted search range in half.
Binary search provides O(log n) worst-case search time when the input is sorted.

detailSections.title: Linear search
paragraphs: Linear search checks each element sequentially.
It is useful when the array is unsorted or when a simple one-time search is required.

detailSections.title: Binary search
paragraphs: Binary search repeatedly cuts the search range in half.
The input must be sorted according to the ordering used by the search.

detailSections.title: How binary search works internally — step by step
bullets: Start with a low and high boundary covering the search range.
Calculate the middle index.
Compare the middle value with the target.
If the target is smaller, search the left half.
If the target is larger, search the right half.
Continue until the target is found or the search range becomes empty.
detailSections.note: Binary search is only reliable when the input is sorted according to the ordering being searched.

paragraphs: Linear search checks elements one by one and takes O(n) in the worst case, so it works on unsorted arrays. Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search range and takes O(log n) in the worst case. I use binary search when the array is sorted and fast repeated lookups are useful.

Multiple constructors can be overloaded using different parameter lists.

object oriented programming (oops).title: Encapsulation and Access Modifiers

Understand why fields are commonly private.
explanation: In one line: encapsulation means keeping an object's internal state controlled and exposing only what callers need.

Members with no modifier have package-private access.

detailSections.title: What is Encapsulation?
paragraphs: Encapsulation means keeping an object's internal state controlled and exposing only the operations that callers need.

Methods can provide controlled access and validate changes before updating internal state.
Getters and setters are useful when direct access is appropriate, but behavior-oriented methods can sometimes provide stronger encapsulation.

explanation: In one line: polymorphism allows one common type or contract to represent different concrete object forms.

detailSections.title: What is Polymorphism?
paragraphs: Polymorphism means one reference or common contract can represent different object forms.

detailSections.title: What is the equals() and hashCode() contract?
paragraphs: The contract defines the relationship between logical equality and hashing.
If two objects are equal according to equals(), their hashCode() values must be identical.
The reverse is not required: two objects with the same hash code do not have to be equal.
The fields used to determine equality should normally be the same fields used to calculate the hash code.
detailSections.note: Remember the key rule: equals() true means hashCode() must match. HashCode() matching does not mean equals() must be true.

explanation: In one line: Comparable allows a class to define its natural ordering through compareTo().

paragraphs: Comparable is an interface used when a class has a natural ordering.
A class implements Comparable<T> and provides the compareTo() method.

Comparator is especially useful with lambda expressions and method references.

type-casting.title: Type Casting Basics
type-casting.summary: Type casting converts a value or reference from one compatible type to another, either implicitly or explicitly.
learningObjectives: Understand widening and narrowing primitive conversions.
Understand upcasting and downcasting with objects.
Differentiate compile-time type from runtime type.
explanation: Type casting is the process of converting a value from one type to another compatible type.
For primitives, casting can change the numeric representation. For objects, casting changes the reference's compile-time view; it does not change the actual object created in memory.
The key interview distinction is compile-time reference type versus runtime object type.

detailSections.title: Simple meaning
paragraphs: If a smaller primitive type is converted to a wider compatible type, Java can usually perform the conversion automatically.
If a wider primitive type is converted to a narrower type, explicit casting is required and information can be lost.
For objects, a child object can be referenced using a parent reference through upcasting. A parent reference can be downcast only when the actual object is compatible with the target child type.
detailSections.note: Casting a reference does not create a new object. It changes how the compiler views the existing reference.

CopyOnWriteArrayList writes create and publish a new array; existing iterators keep their old snapshot.
Exact ArrayList growth is an implementation detail, not a List API promise.
